clue.text: Hand over alcohol — it'll help when leaving the EU

definitions.text: it'll help when leaving the EU

parts.note: to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A cheeky bribe of booze to smooth a departure from the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests slipping a bottle to a customs officer; in fact the two opening ideas are simply joined, and the rest is a whimsical description of the document.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description by function rather than a synonym: after Brexit, Britons need the document stamped at EU borders.

clue.text: Shame about a Republican's correspondence

indicators.note: 'About' in the sense of around: the shame word stands round the A and R.

explanation.surface: Disgrace surrounding a political party member's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' pretends to mean letters, but here it means equivalence or matching, as between two currencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality, and the close correspondence between two values, as with currencies at par, is a matter of parity.

clue.text: Thought son cut speed round the bend

indicators.note: 'Round the bend' is slang for crazy, and crazed letters don't stay in their order.

explanation.surface: A driver's son slowed down as he took a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' reads as a stretch of road, which is why it hides so well after 'cut speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb: 'I suspected as much' means 'I thought as much', a close synonym.

clue.text: Her pilot, up in the air, wanting love? This could help

indicators.note: Things up in the air are tossed about and come down in a new order.

parts.note: love = O, zero in tennis; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A woman whose airborne pilot is lonely, and something that might win him over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends by pointing at itself: the answer is exactly what someone wanting love might need. 'Up in the air' fits the pilot but stirs the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a philtre is a love potion, the kind of thing that helps someone whose love life is lacking.

clue.text: Compass needle moving right to the start

indicators.note: R is right, and moving it to the start takes the last letter round to the front.

parts.note: to needle someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A compass needle swinging round to point back to where it began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass needle' looks like one object; split it into definition and wordplay. Nothing is lost in the move: the R leaves the end and rejoins at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass is an old sense meaning extent or scope, as in 'within the compass of' a plan or a singer's voice.

clue.text: Evil spirits disturbed Slough

indicators.note: Something disturbed has been knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged.

explanation.surface: Evil spirits have unsettled the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, much mocked in poetry and on TV; the capital letter makes it look like a place, not raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghouls come from Arabic folklore as grave-robbing demons, so they fit evil spirits as a plain synonym.

clue.text: Composer with sign of hesitation — piece could be removed from here

definitions.text: piece could be removed from here

parts.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer hesitates over which piece of music to drop from a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: With a composer about, 'piece' means a work of music; here it is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: 'piece' is gangster slang for a handgun, and a holster is where it is drawn from.

clue.text: Golf club missing head, say

indicators.note: A word's head is its first letter, and here that letter is missing.

explanation.surface: A putter whose head has come off, as a golfer might describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: A club missing its head is a real mishap on the course; here the head is only the first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to utter a word is to say it aloud.

clue.text: Shooting pain's beginning in gardening activity

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: seeding is sowing seed, a gardening job

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word pain, whose first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A gardener feels a stabbing pain while working in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' looks like it describes the pain, but it is the definition. P goes inside SEEDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting along means going very fast, i.e. speeding.

clue.text: Bird food

definitions.meaning: bird is British rhyming slang (bird-lime = time) for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Seed for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'bird' and 'porridge' are British slang for time served in prison; the surface wants a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: porridge is a breakfast of oats, and British slang for a prison sentence, which 'bird' also means.

clue.text: Euro result isn't fantastic — embracing America is a risky game to play

indicators.note: Arms embracing someone go round them, so the rearranged letters wrap round the A.
Fantastic in the sense of fanciful: the letters are reshaped into something unreal.

explanation.surface: A disappointing Euro football result, and taking on the Americans is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Euros are the European football championship, so the surface is a sports report; the fodder spans most of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the game of spinning a revolver with one bullet and firing at your own head.

clue.text: Regularly acts in that place

indicators.note: in means these letters are put inside the next word
regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the word acts, whose alternate letters are wanted

explanation.surface: A troupe performs in the same venue night after night.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is also the definition: a theatre is the place where acts are put on regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where plays are performed and actors appear on stage regularly.

clue.text: Went to bed really missing friend and bored

indicators.note: missing means the word really goes without the letters for friend

parts.note: tired, as in tired of something, means bored

explanation.surface: Someone without company and with nothing to do simply went to bed early.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is a formal way of saying someone went to sleep.

clue.text: Is losing first hair? Editor's anxious

indicators.note: takes the cut letters out of the word

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An editor fretting about losing hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether someone is balding; 'losing first' only removes one letter from the short word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern synonym: someone stressed is tense and worried, as is someone anxious.

clue.text: Nip inside branch for business chat

indicators.note: 'Inside' puts the nip word within the branch word.

parts.note: a stalk is a plant's branch or stem
to nip or hop somewhere is to go quickly

explanation.surface: Popping into a local branch of a firm to discuss work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' suggests a bank or shop outlet, which fits the business chat; it is a plant stem.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'talking shop' is discussing your work, so shop talk is chat about business.

clue.text: Be in power shower, by the sound of it

indicators.note: Judged by its sound, not its spelling: the word heard is spelt another way.

explanation.surface: Standing under a power shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power shower' is a strong bathroom shower; split it so that 'Be in power' is the definition and 'shower' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigns holds the throne, so 'be in power' is a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Separation, to a lion, is upsetting

indicators.note: Upsetting something tips it over and jumbles it, so the letters are rearranged.

explanation.surface: Being parted from its pride distresses a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' reads as emotional distress for the lion, which is why it passes as part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: isolation is the state of being set apart from others.

clue.text: Bearing gifts for the listener

indicators.note: What matters to a listener is sound, so the answer is heard like the gift word.

explanation.surface: Arriving with gifts for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing gifts' reads as carrying presents, as the three wise men did; 'Bearing' is a noun, meaning someone's manner or poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing in the sense of dignified carriage; a person with presence has a commanding manner.

clue.text: More coarse fish almost about to return

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the rudd is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: to return means turning back, so these letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A rather crude fish is nearly ready to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More coarse' hints at coarse fishing, which is where the rudd, a freshwater fish, comes in; but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruder is the comparative of rude, meaning cruder or more vulgar, so more coarse.

clue.text: Dull relative? That is very impolite, ultimately

indicators.note: Ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is taken.

explanation.surface: Complaining that a boring relative is extremely rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull relative' reads as a boring family member; 'Dull' is a verb, as in dulling pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller dulls an ache, so 'dull' as a verb matches the sense of easing pain.

clue.text: One who gives talks about parking next to European driver

indicators.note: 'About' means around: the speaker word stands round the two letters.

explanation.surface: A speaker lecturing on parking beside a European motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' pulls towards cars; here it means anyone who runs a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine, crane or train is its operator, so driver fits as a generic description.

clue.text: Makes a request of one eating fruit? On the contrary

indicators.note: Something eating takes another inside it.
'On the contrary' flips the roles, so the fruit swallows the one.

explanation.surface: Asking something of a person who is snacking on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips who eats whom: it is the fruit that swallows the one, not the one the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply for a job or grant is to make a formal request for it.

clue.text: Starts where thespians might be

definitions.meaning: split into two words, this places actors on a stage or film set

explanation.surface: The points at which actors begin their work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning needs the answer split in two: actors are on sets while they work.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: onsets are beginnings, and split as 'on sets' it places actors on film or stage sets.

clue.text: Red mark lethal? Not half!

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound

indicators.note: not half means half the word is left out, here its back half

parts.note: the word lethal, of which only the first half stays

explanation.surface: A red mark is asked whether it is deadly, and the reply is an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for a strong yes, but here it says LETHAL loses HAL to give LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Occupy Vietnam? US endeavoured, to an extent

indicators.note: 'To an extent' means partly, so the answer is only part of the words that hide it.

explanation.surface: Did the US partly try to occupy Vietnam?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupy' looks military next to Vietnam; it means keep someone entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym in the sense of keeping someone busy: toys occupy a child by entertaining it.

clue.text: England player perhaps cheers — not out, skipper!

parts.note: an international player is a cap, from the cap awarded
in cricket, a batsman not out is still in

explanation.surface: Congratulating an England cricket captain who is still batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and 'ta' are both British for thanks; 'not out' is the cricket term for a batsman still at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: skipper is the informal word for whoever leads a team or commands a boat.

clue.text: Hide status? No time

indicators.note: 'No time' means without T, so that letter comes out.

explanation.surface: Questioning whether prestige matters when time is short.
explanation.walkthrough: Cachet means prestige or status; 'Hide' is a noun or verb here, not an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, and as a verb to cache something is to stash it away.

clue.text: Cook in US: I've no clue about the French type of cooking

indicators.note: 'About' means around: the rearranged letters stand round the French word.
To cook the books is to tamper with them, so the letters are doctored into a new order.

explanation.surface: An American cook admitting ignorance of French cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person in the kitchen; it is the instruction to stir the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of cooking rather than a synonym: the 1970s French school of light, prettily plated dishes.

clue.text: Still following the Spanish team

indicators.note: 'Following' puts the still word after the Spanish word.

explanation.surface: Continuing to support the Spanish national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still following' reads as loyal fandom, and 'Still' as 'yet'; it is the intensifier in 'still better'.
explanation.definitionFit: A number used as a noun: football and cricket sides field eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Most of a piece of cake eaten by poor farm workers

indicators.note: eaten by means the shortened word goes inside

parts.note: pants is British slang for poor quality

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a piece of cake means something easy

explanation.surface: Poor farm hands eating most of a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means rubbish or poor quality, and 'a piece of cake' is an idiom for something simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are rural labourers who work the land.
